name: Operating Systems & Processes
description: Understand how operating systems manage processes, memory, files, and resources from a developer perspective.

cards.back: Software that manages hardware resources and provides services to applications.
A running instance of a program with its own memory and state.
A unit of execution within a process.

cards.front: Why do operating systems schedule processes?
cards.back: To fairly share CPU time between tasks.
An abstraction that allows programs to use more memory than physically available.
Saving and restoring process state to switch execution.
Busy loops, heavy computation, or too many active processes.
Input/output operations like disk and network access.

cards.front: Why is disk slower than memory?
cards.back: Because physical storage has higher latency.
A handle representing an open file or stream.
Due to invalid memory access or unhandled errors.
Running multiple processes seemingly at the same time.
A measure of runnable and waiting processes.

cards.front: Why do developers need OS knowledge?
cards.back: To debug performance, reliability, and security issues.

sampleIdeas.name: What an OS Really Does
sampleIdeas.textDescription:
Operating systems coordinate hardware and software.

They manage CPU, memory, files, and devices.

Understanding this clarifies many bugs.

Abstractions matter.

sampleIdeas.name: Processes, Threads, and Performance
sampleIdeas.textDescription:
Processes isolate programs.

Threads enable concurrency.

Performance issues often stem from misuse.

Observation beats guessing.

sampleIdeas.name: Memory and Crashes Explained
sampleIdeas.textDescription:
Memory is finite.

Leaks and invalid access crash programs.

Virtual memory hides complexity.

Tools reveal reality.
